subject: Climate & Environment
title: Marine Protected Areas
description: A fast breakdown of Marine Protected Areas for builders.

hook.text: Only about 8% of the ocean is currently protected. Scientists say we need at least 30%.

buildup.text: Marine protected areas ban or limit fishing, drilling, and mining in designated zones.

discovery.text: Inside well-managed MPAs, fish populations double and biodiversity increases significantly.

twist.text: Most existing MPAs allow some fishing. Only 3% of the ocean is fully no-take protected.

climax.text: The 2022 High Seas Treaty opened the door to protecting international waters for the first time.

punchline.text: The ocean needs parks just like the land does. It's finally getting some.

quiz.question: What percentage of the ocean is fully no-take protected?

details.summary: Marine protected areas restrict human activity in designated ocean zones to conserve biodiversity and allow ecosystems to recover. Only about eight percent of the global ocean is currently protected, and less than three percent is fully no-take, far short of the 30 percent target set for 2030.
details.whyItMatters: MPAs are proven to boost fish populations, restore habitats, and increase ecosystem resilience. Expanding and enforcing them is essential for reversing decades of ocean degradation.
takeaways: About eight percent of the ocean is currently protected
Less than three percent is fully closed to extraction
The global target is 30 percent protection by 2030

faq.question: Do marine protected areas work?
faq.answer: When well-enforced, MPAs dramatically increase fish biomass, species diversity, and organism size within their boundaries. Benefits spill over to adjacent fishing grounds through larval export and adult movement, supporting both ecology and local fisheries.

faq.question: Why is so little of the ocean protected?
faq.answer: Opposition from fishing and extractive industries, lack of enforcement resources, jurisdictional complexity in international waters, and insufficient funding all limit MPA expansion. The high-seas treaty adopted in 2023 aims to close governance gaps.
